steps.text: When you first open Curator's Vault, read the Terms of Service and scroll to the bottom.
Then tap Privacy Policy, and scroll that to the bottom too.
Tap I Accept & Continue.
A short welcome shows what you can do. Tap Continue.
Every kind of piece starts on. Tap one to turn it off if you don't collect it. Then tap Continue.
Type the name you want on your Home screen, or leave it blank. Tap Get Started.
You're on Home. Identify, Add Item, Tools, Settings, and Wish List are one tap away.
The tabs at the bottom take you to Home, My Collection, Tools, and Settings.
To change the language, tap Settings.
Scroll down and tap Language.
Pick a language. Each one is shown in its own words, like Español for Spanish.
The whole app switches right away. To switch back, pick English.
Back in English.

chapters.title: Identify a piece from a photo

steps.text: To find out what a piece is, tap Identify a piece on Home.
Pick what kind of piece it is. Here it's a coin, so tap Coin.
Tap Take Photo with the piece in front of you, or Choose Photo to use one you already have.
Pick the photo.
A photo of the other side helps with the date and mint mark. Here there's one side, so tap Obverse only.
Scroll down and tap Identify.
In a moment you have the report: what it is, the year, the grade, and a price estimate.
Asking prices from similar pieces for sale give you a second check.
Below, fix anything that's wrong before you save. Here, the series becomes Morgan Dollar.
Tap Save to Vault, then Save.
Tap View in vault. The piece is in your collection, with its photo and value.
To add a piece by hand, tap Add Item on Home.
Your collection opens. Tap the round add button.
Pick the kind of piece. Coins is already picked.
Fill in what you know. Here, the denomination, the year, and the series.
Scroll down to Estimated Value and type what it's worth.
Type what you paid under Purchase price.
Tap Save Item. The piece is in your vault, and the vault total goes up.
Tap My Collection to see every piece you own. The top shows what your vault is worth.
Tap a kind of piece to see only those.
Type in the search box to find a piece by name.
Wish and For Sale keep the pieces you want and the ones you're selling. Tap Owned to come back.
Tap a piece to open it, with its photo, value, and details.
Silver and gold coins show what their metal is worth today. Tap My Collection, then the coin.
Scroll down to Worth today. The metal value uses today's silver price, and updates every day.
To hear when it changes, type a price under More than or Less than.
Tap Save alert. You get a notification when the value crosses your price.
Keep a list of the pieces you're hunting. On Home, tap Wish List.
Tap Add Item.
Pick the kind of piece, then fill in what you're after: the country, the year, and the series.
Pick a priority, and type the most you'd pay under Target Price.
Tap Save. The piece is on your list, and your budget adds up at the top.
To hear when a wish-list piece comes up for sale, tap Tools, then Price alerts.
Tap + New.
Pick the piece from your wish list, and type the most you'd pay.
Tap Create. Tap Check all any time to look for matches now.
To weigh two pieces side by side, tap Tools, then Compare.
Pick the kind of piece. Type a name in the search box and tap Search.
Tap the first piece, then the second.
Value, price range, and rarity line up next to each other.
To track a set you're building, tap Tools, then Set completion.
Tap Add a set, and pick the set.
Coins you already own count right away. You see how many you have, and how many to go.
Tap the set for the count.
To keep a record of a piece's condition, tap Tools, then Condition.
Tap Tap to select an item, and pick the piece.
Tap Create New Assessment.
Pick the grade and the condition, and add a note.
Tap Save. Each check is kept, so you can see changes over time.

chapters.title: Keep cert numbers with your pieces

steps.text: To keep a grading certificate or appraisal with a piece, tap Tools, then Cert tracker.
Tap the add button, and pick the piece.
Pick the kind of certificate and who issued it. Type the number and the grade.
Type the appraised value.
Tap Add Certification. Totals at the top add up your appraised value.
Sending pieces off for grading? Tap Tools, then Grading queue.
Tap Add First Submission.
Pick the grading company, and type the order number.
Type what you sent, and what it costs.
Tap Save. Move it along as it's received, graded, and shipped back.
A passport is a one-page record of a piece, with a QR code. Tap Tools, then Collectible passport.
Tap Tap to select an item, and pick the piece.
The card shows the year, grade, condition, and value.
At the bottom, tap Share Passport to send it, or Print Passport.
To date a Zippo lighter, tap Tools, then Zippo decoder.
Type the letters and numbers from the bottom stamp, or tap an example.
Tap Decode. You get the month and year it was made.
Back up your vault before a show or a new phone. Tap Settings, scroll down, and tap Back up now.
It saves your whole vault as one backup file.
The file is in your phone's backup folder. Backup files aren't password-protected, so keep a copy somewhere secure, such as your cloud drive or account.
